approach: Find the applied force at t = 2 s and the maximum friction the surface can supply, then check that the applied force has not yet reached that maximum.

steps.text: Find the size of the applied force at t = 2 s.
Find the maximum friction force the surface can supply, using the normal force, which equals the block's weight on this horizontal plane.
Since the applied force, 4 N, is smaller than the maximum friction, 8 N, the block is still at rest, and friction matches the applied force to keep it still.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming friction is always at its maximum value once any force is applied, without checking whether the block has actually started moving, gives f = μmg = 8 N.
